name: rf-quadrupole-unconfined
description: An ideal RF quadrupole at 1 mbar, described as a density rather than as trajectories. The pair of these two examples is the point: they are the same model with one number changed - the drive amplitude - and each half matches a DIFFERENT closed form. Neither is worth much alone, because a width that happens to match one formula proves nothing about whether the drive is doing anything. The field is analytic rather than solved, which is what makes the expectations arithmetic: a solved rod geometry departs from the ideal quadrupole by a few per cent, and writing the ideal formula against it would assert a modelling difference as though it were exact. With the drive at zero the field vanishes identically and the packet spreads by diffusion alone, to sqrt(seed^2 + 2 D t) with D = mu kT / q from the Einstein relation. It reaches 1.303 mm against the confined case's 0.137 - nine times wider, on a model that differs in one number. The drive frequency is still declared and still positive, because a zero frequency is a static field wearing a drive's clothes and is refused; what is zero here is the amplitude, which is the honest way to say the generator is off.
